# Establishment log — bardo-thodol-012 (pp. 107–115), 2026-11-23

This part is the fourth in text **ga**. It runs from the southern six Īśvarīs at 107.3, through the western and northern six and the four gatekeeper yoginīs. Then comes the teaching that the 58 blood-drinkers are one's own projection (dharmakāya: empty aspect → peaceful, clear aspect → wrathful). The sizes of the deities follow. Last come Yama, Lord of Death, who appears to the one who does not recognise, and the call on the yidam by name.
There is no transcription of this print for ga. Three readers (all on the strongest model; no Sonnet role ran) read the images line by line from scratch, with the other recension (readings/witness_ga.txt) open only as a guide:
- Reader A read 107.3–109.
- Reader B read 110–112.
- Reader C read 113–115 and looked at 116.1.

Both seams are clean: 109.5/110.1 joins སེར་མོ་|རའི་མགོ, and 112.5/113.1 joins …འཆར་རོ༔|ཁྲོ་བོའི. The full tables are in readings/read_A-log.md, read_B-log.md and read_C-log.md. The editor (this firing) looked at the 112.3 gap again at ×5 on a straightened copy. It could not read it either; the traces look like ལ་ཡར་ཇ…བསུས/བཞུས, possibly a correction cut into the block.

## Layout
- Every page has five lines.
- pp. 109, 111, 113 and 115 are leaf fronts and open with the ornament, written ༄༅༔ ༔.
- The images are skewed by 1.0–2.0°, so they were read from straightened copies.
- **Start.** The part starts on 107.3 with ཀྱཻ་རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ ལྷོ་ནས, after 011's …དེ་ལ་མ་འཇིགས་ཤིག༔.
- **End.** The part ends mid-line on 115.5 at …ཡི་དམ་རིན་པོ་ཆེ་ཞེས་བོས་ལ་གསོལ་བ་ཐོབ་ཅིག༔, which closes the call on the yidam.
  - **Part 013 begins mid-line on 115.5** with ཁྱོད་རང་གི་བླ་མའི་…, the call on the lama, which closes on 116.1 with …ཐུགས་རྗེས་མ་བཏང་བར་གྱིས་ལ་གསོལ་བ་ཐོབ་ཅིག༔. C read 116.1 at ×3 only, so part 013's reader must confirm it.

## A gap set aside (README rule 7)
- **112.3**, in the sentence རང་སྣང་དུ་ངོ་ཤེས་པར་གྱིས་[…]་ཤིག༔. Between གྱིས and ཤིག the print has about six or seven letters that no reader could read. The other recension has nothing there.
  - B's traces, left to right: a ལ-like letter, a ཡ-like letter, ར, a ཇ-shaped letter, ག/བ, a letter with a ུ, ས.
  - The letters are **left out of the established text**, which reads ངོ་ཤེས་པར་གྱིས་ཤིག༔, a complete sentence.
  - The draft must put a `gap` on that unit, saying that a few syllables after གྱིས on p. 112 l. 3 are unread, and add a matching entry to gaps.json. They should also be recorded in QUESTIONS.md.

## Doubtful readings marked [?] (11 marks)
- 107.3 ཕ in ཕ[?]་ཝད་མགོ (its tick could be a fused tsheg, which would give པ). See "Kept".
- 109.4 རི in སྒོ་མ་རི[?]་རྣལ་འབྱོར་མ་བཞི: a stray syllable that the other recension lacks. Perhaps a dittography of the ར of རྣལ. Note only.
- 111.2 བྲེད (other recension བྲེད; fits the traces).
- 112.4 སང in དེ་སང[?]་རེས (other recension ད་རེས "this time"). Note only; the sense is probably "this time".
- 113.4 མཁའ in ནམ་མཁའ (other recension ནམ་མཁའི་མཐའ).
- 113.5 ཡོང (or འོང; the print has ཡོང་ངོ at 114.2).
- 114.1 འཐུང in ཀླད་པ་འཐུང་བ.
- 114.2 པར in སྐྲག་པར་མ་བྱེད.
- 114.3 གཟུགས in སྟོང་ཉིད་རང་གཟུགས.
- 114.4 དངོས (the first letter looks more like ག). See the misprint below.
- 115.4 ཐོན in མཚན་ནས་གང་ཐོན་བོས་ཅིག ("call by name whatever comes"). Unusual; the other recension has only མཚན་ནས་བོས་ཤིག.
- Part 011's སྤྲའི[?] at 107.5 is withdrawn. A read it at ×8: the letter is ཝ, one letter high and not a stack, so the line reads ཝའི་མགོ "fox-headed", as in the other recension.

## Fixes (11)
- Eight are missing tshegs:
  - line joins: 108.3/4 ལག་གཉིས|མདའ, 111.1/2 འཐུང|གི, 111.4/5 ཀྱཻ|རིགས, 112.4/5 ཡིད|ལ, 113.1/2 ཀྱཻ|རིགས, 113.2/3 ཤེས|ན and 113.3/4 པོའི|སྐུ;
  - mid-line: 109.2 ལག་ན|མཆེ, at the start of the line after the ornament.
  - At 112.4/5 the print sets the tsheg at the start of 112.5 rather than after ཡིད; it is not in the file.
- One contraction is written out: 111.3 འགྲོག། → འགྲོ་གོ། (one o-sign over two letters).
- **Two misprints are corrected (rule 5b; the notes must give the print's reading):**
  - 110.4/5 ཆ་ལ་|ལས → ཆ་ལས: ལ is set twice across the line end ("from the clear aspect"). Certain.
  - 114.4 དངོས[?]་པ་ཅན་དུ → དངོས་པོ་ཅན་དུ ("substantial"): the o-sign is dropped. Only དངོས་པོ་ཅན makes sense. The first letter is doubtful (it may be ག); the note says so.

## Kept, note only (the editor did not correct these: each needs a whole word changed or added, which is beyond a letter-level misprint, or the reading is not certain)
- **107.3 ཕ[?]་ཝད་མགོ**, the head of the first southern goddess. No such word exists. ཕ་ཝང "bat" is one letter off, and the other recension has ཕག "sow". Moderate to low certainty. The note should give "perhaps for ཕ་ཝང 'bat'". The goddess is named དགའ་བ here, where the other recension has རྡོ་རྗེ.
- **109.5 ཤར་ནས་རྡོ་རྗེ་ཕག་མོ་ཁུ་བྱུག་མགོ**. The other recension has the colour དཀར་མོ "white" where this print has ཕག་མོ. It is perhaps copied from 109.1's ཕག་མོ. As printed: "Vajra-Sow, cuckoo-headed".
- **110.4 ཆོས་སྐུ་གསལ་བའི་ཆ་ལས་ཁྲོ་བའི་ལྷ**. The sense and the other recension want ལོངས་སྐུ (sambhogakāya) for the clear aspect, opposite ཆོས་སྐུ for the empty aspect in the sentence before. The print repeats ཆོས་སྐུ. The note says so; the text is as printed.
- **111.2–3 སྡུག་བསྔལ་གྱི་སྣོན་མར་འགྲོ་གོ** (after the contraction is written out). The reading is obscure. B suggests གྱིས་ནོན་པར་འགྲོ་གོ "go oppressed by suffering"; the other recension's wording should be given in the note. Mark the sense as uncertain.
- **111.5 ཐ་མ་ཡང་རང་བཅོ་བརྒྱད་བརྩེགས་པ་ཙམ**. It lacks ལུས ("eighteen times one's own body stacked"). The sense still holds.
- **113.3 རང་སྣང་དུ་ངོ་ཤེས་ན་ཤི་མ་ཐག་ཏུ…གཤིན་རྗེ…སྐུ་འཆར་རོ**. The context (Yama appears to one who fails to recognise) and the other recension (ངོ་མ་ཤེས་ན) want the negative. The image clearly has no མ (×7). The note must say that the print lacks the negative and that the sense needs it. Keep the translation as printed in `l`, and make the problem explicit in `i` or the note.
- **115.2 དེ་ལྟར་ངོ་ཤེས་ན་ནི་ཡི་དམ་གྱི་ལྷ་ཡིན་ནོ** (other recension དེ་ལྟར་མ་ཤེས་ནའང). It reads well as printed.
- 108.5: the wind goddess རླུང་ལྷ is སྦྲུལ་གྱི་མགོ "snake-headed" (other recension "wolf-headed"), so the north has two snake heads (109.3 ཆུ་ལྷ too).
- 114.3 ཞེད་མི་དགོས (other recension བྲེད་སྔངས་མི་དགོས), and 115.5 ར་མདའ་ལ་རྒྱུག་ཅིག "run to [my] aid" (other recension ར་མདའ་མཛོད་ཅིག).
- ཀྱཻ is printed with two e-signs, as in 011. དངངས is the print's spelling.

## Where the print differs in sense from the other recension (the print is followed)
- Colours: 107.4 ཟླ་བ་དམར་མོ (other recension དཀར་མོ), 108.1 ཟ་བ་དམར་ལྗང (ལྗང་ནག), 108.2 སྟོབས་ཆེན་དམར་མོ (དཀར་མོ), 108.3 སྲིན་མོ་སེར་མོ (དམར་མོ), 108.4 ནོར་སྲུང་ལྗང་ཁུ (དམར་ལྗང).
- 108.3/4 ལག་གཉིས་མདའ་གཞུ་འགེངས་པ "draws the bow and arrow with both hands" (other recension ལག་ན).
- 109.3 ལག་ན་བེ་ཅོན་ཐོགས་ཤིང་ཁྲག་འཐུང་བ "holds a club and drinks blood" (other recension "holds a great corpse and drinks blood from a skull").
- 109.4 lacks "listen without distraction".
- 110.5/111.1 ཐོན་ནས་ཤར་འཆར་བའི and 111.1 རང་མདངས༔ རང་ཤར་བར་ཤེས་ནས. 111.3 lacks ཚོགས. 112.2 lacks རང་མདངས་རང་ before འོད་དང་སྐུ. 112.3 has འོད་གསལ་རང་གི་རང་མདངས (other recension རང་རིག). 112.4 lacks ཞེས. 112.5 has སྐྲག་ནས (other recension སྐྲག་ན).
- 113.3 has ཆོས་ཉིད་ཀྱི་བར་དོར. 114.1 ཁམས་ཐམས་ཅད་ཁེངས་ནས་ཡོང་ངོ "comes filling all the world-realms" (other recension ཁམས་གང་ནས). 114.3 སྟོང་ཉིད་རང་གཟུགས (other recension སྟོང་པའི). 114.4 སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱིས་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ལ, with agent and object reversed.
- 115.1 ཐག་ཆོད་ན (other recension ཤེས་ན). 115.4 ཡི་དམ་གང་ཡིན་པ without གྱི་ལྷ.
